notes:
Summary: Halo is a platform used by 120+ enterprise contact centers to automate agent workflows. Primary interest = tool-calling to downstream systems (Zendesk, ServiceNow, internal ticket API) for create/update workflows, plus refund orchestration via Stripe/Adyen APIs and escalation toggles to PagerDuty. Key asks: 
- Must log every action to customer audit log (immutable) and Redwood audit events for compliance.
- Refunds: require reversible flow and manual approval fallback for amounts > $500; idempotency + cross-service saga patterns.
- Spike resilience: typical peak is 4k concurrent agent sessions; expected 150-200 tps for ticket create/updates during campaigns. Need graceful degradation (queue + lightweight model fallback) so agent UI not blocked.
- Security: SAML SSO, SCIM for user sync, KMS integration for key rotation, per-tenant data residency controls (EU customers), retention policies, signed webhooks.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns per route; tracing link from agent UI to model inference + downstream API call; error analytics for failed tool calls.

Notes from call (shorthand):
- "If the model tries to submit refund without approval, we need a hard stop + audit record" — product.
- Concern about retries: current middleware performs 3x retry with exponential backoff; need control over retry policy and circuit-breaker between Redwood and payment gateway.
- L2 Escalation: Want automatic PagerDuty trigger if ticket update fails 2x or contains high-risk tag.
- Compliance team requires a 3rd-party pentest report before on-prem sign-off.

Links: POC deck + security Q&A (drive links), transcript ff_2026-02-22_call_45b1c2. Gmail threads with legal/pricing back-and-forth. Jira support keys opened for performance clarifications (SUPPORT-8721, SUPPORT-8799).
summary: Enterprise contact-center vendor evaluating Redwood for agent-assist + tool-calling. Priority: safe/refundable tool-calls, auditability, surge reliability, and VPC/on-prem deployment options. POC requested to validate throughput, retry semantics, and SAML integration.
